title: Simultaneous common-stage descent of rational Weil operation diagrams
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$ use the rational category $D^b_c(T,E)$ and the common-stage category $D^b_c(T,\Omega)$, whose Hom groups are the filtered colimits over finite coefficient extensions [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Weil objects are $(M,\theta_M:P_TM\simeq M)$ with arbitrary rational isomorphisms, not specified integral lifts [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

Take finitely many separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and separated finite-type morphisms between them. Consider any finite collection of objects and rational arrows in their common-stage categories, including specified Weil isomorphisms and their inverses. Allow finitely many expressions in these objects and arrows formed using $P_T$, shifts, canonical Tate twists [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], $Lf^*$, $Rf_*$, $Rf_!$, derived tensor and internal Hom, on their bounded constructible domains; any first variable required to be site-perfect is site-perfect [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Retain the canonical tensor, Hom, shift, evaluation, transposition, projection and ordinary adjunction comparisons [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts, lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation, lem-pod-constructible-mate-coherence]. For smooth $f$ of pure dimension $d\ge0$, also allow the canonical purity family $\gamma_{f,M}:Lf^*M(d)[2d]\simeq Rf^!M$, the constructible exceptional adjunction and its right mate of inverse compact-support exchange, and the trace $\varepsilon_{f,M}Rf_!(\gamma_{f,M})$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, def-pur-smooth-trace]; use compactifications defined over $k_0$ and the canonical rational realization [def-pur-canonical-rational-purity-realization, lem-pur-rational-weil-naturality-mate]. At $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ also allow finitely many cohomology vectors represented by $\Lambda_s\to N[r]$ and their canonical point transports [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-frobenius-point-transport].

There is one finite coefficient extension $L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$ representing all the chosen data simultaneously, such that the inverse Weil arrows are actual inverses over $L$, every expression is identified with the same expression on the $L$-representatives, and every listed canonical comparison, evaluation, transpose, purity map, exceptional mate and trace is represented by its specified $L$-map under these identifications. Any finite list of equalities of these expressions valid in the common-stage categories holds over a further single finite extension. Conversely, any equality between such expressions established over a common finite extension gives the corresponding equality of common-stage morphism classes, independently of the chosen representatives and of further extension.

For point expressions the identifications carry $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_N)\iota_N$ to the same finite-stage exchange-then-Weil-datum action and carry the coefficient-unit datum to the canonical unit datum. Consequently finite-stage identities involving these actions and the degreewise values of a derived pairing pass to the common-stage cohomology vectors, with the original ordinary and compact-support factors retained separately. No stable integral lattice is asserted or needed.

source.place: Proof sentences 3 and 4 final clause; retained rational proof Step 11, simultaneous coefficient descent including inverse Weil arrows and point transports

proof.text: For each chosen object choose its displayed pair $(E,K)$. Choose a finite-stage representative of each chosen arrow, including both directions of each Weil isomorphism and each point vector. There are finitely many fields: repeatedly take composita to obtain $L_0$ containing them all, taking $\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the empty list. Extend every representative to $L_0$. For an object initially at $E$, the common-stage identification with $(L_0,K\otimes_E L_0)$ is represented by the identity at $L_0$, using the scalar unit and associator. Thus these choices identify the original endpoints, not just their isomorphism classes.

source.place: Finite-field assembly for the operation and comparison assertions, sentences 1–2.

proof.text: Write $u:P_TM\to M$ and $v:M\to P_TM$ for the chosen representatives. The equalities $uv=1_M$ and $vu=1_{P_TM}$ hold in the common-stage Hom groups. Their defining eventual-equality criterion supplies a finite extension witnessing each equation. Take the compositum of these finitely many witnesses and $L_0$, obtaining $L_1$; all equations persist because scalar extension preserves composition and identities. The $L_1$ arrows are now actual inverses. For each first variable required to be site-perfect, include beforehand a finite-field site-perfect representative and the two arrows of its common-stage isomorphism to the chosen object, and enforce their inverse equations in the same way. Scalar extension preserves the local bounded finite-projective description: extend its splitting $e^2=e$ on a finite sum of units and its bounded differential. Hence all required site-perfect domains hold at $L_1$.

source.place: Finite-field realization of the Weil data in sentence 2, retaining the stated operation domains.

proof.text: Evaluate the finite expression trees from their leaves upward over $L_1$. At a unary operation use its specified scalar comparison; at tensor or internal Hom first extend both arguments to the same field. If $c_{A,L}:S_{L/E}(A_E)\simeq A_L$ denotes the resulting endpoint comparison, the representative of an arrow expression $w:A\to B$ is $c_{B,L}^{-1}w_Lc_{A,L}$. For internal Hom the first input arrow is reversed, exactly as in its defining formula. Composition cancels the intermediate $c$ and $c^{-1}$. Shifts use the actual shift comparison, and twists use the canonical coefficient line and its Weil datum, not a chosen trivialization. The comparisons $c$ are, for pullback (including $P_T$), tensor and internal Hom, the scalar-extension comparisons of the operation definition, whose naturality, identity-extension and tower cocycles are those of the integral operation scalar-extension lemma, localized; for $Rf_*$ the comparison $b$ of the ordinary-adjunction scalar lemma; for $Rf_!$ the compact-support comparison $q$ of the exceptional-adjunction coefficient lemma, applicable because every integral representative is finite-Tor (step 5). With these comparisons the descent lemma gives the representative formulas; the field-operation lifts give the Weil formulas $F(\theta)a$, $(\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu$ and $R\mathcal Hom(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h$. The coefficient cocycles make this recursive identification compatible with further extension. Restrict throughout to the bounded constructible domains stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Sentences 1–2: operations and their specified Weil structures, assembled at one field.

proof.text: Under these endpoint identifications, retain the specified canonical comparisons rather than descending unrelated arrows with the same endpoints. For $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ the ordinary-adjunction scalar lemma gives $h_L(C(u)a_M^{-1})=b_KC(h_E(u))$ and its inverse form; with $u=1_{Lf^*M}$, $v=1_{Rf_*K}$ these are the unit and counit squares $b_{Lf^*M}C(\eta_M)=Rf_{L*}(a_M^{-1})\eta_{CM}$ and $\varepsilon_{CK}Lf_L^*(b_K)a_{Rf_*K}=C(\varepsilon_K)$, and adjuncts are independent of the common field. The pullback-scalar bridge identifies its ordinary comparison $a$ with the strict-tower pullback comparison under $\chi$. These are the supplied data of the exchange/projection definition, which forms the common-field components from them. Its projection map is the stated unit–tensor–counit composite, so substitution of those squares gives the same projection component over $L_1$. For Hom use the specified evaluation-normalized scalar comparison: its transpose is scalar extension of evaluation, as asserted by the Hom-scalar lemma. Hence evaluation is represented by evaluation and, by the tensor-Hom bijection, the transpose is represented by the transpose at the same field. Frobenius Hom/evaluation/shift comparisons use the reindexing coefficient-descent lemma. The mate-transport lemma applies to the supplied scalar-compatible adjunction maps and comparisons; its three-factor formula gives the specified mate after extension. These are identities on all localized arrows, including the arbitrary rational $\theta$ and its inverse chosen in step 2.

source.place: Sentence 2: evaluations, adjunction maps, exchanges and projection maps; canonical comparison normalization.

proof.text: For each smooth $f$, use the canonical rational purity realization, with its coefficient-unit orientation and its actual tensor/line/pullback/shift source comparison. The normalized rational purity-diagram lemma gives the coefficient square $b\,S(\gamma_E)=\gamma_L a$ on every rational input; it explicitly places integral representatives in the needed uniform finite-Tor domain. The smooth-operation identification transfers this square through the framework/PBC coefficient equivalences, keeping scalar unitors and shift comparisons. Thus the common-stage $\gamma$ is represented by this specified $\gamma_{L_1}$, with its inverse represented by $\gamma_{L_1}^{-1}$. The exceptional-adjunction coefficient identities carry the unit and counit to the specified ones. Consequently the three-factor right mate of inverse compact exchange and the composite $\varepsilon\,Rf_!(\gamma)$ are represented by those very finite-stage formulas. The rational Weil naturality/mate lemma identifies the former with the prescribed Frobenius comparison for purity; its compactification hypothesis holds because the retained compactifications are defined over $k_0$. This argument uses rational isomorphisms only, not integral Weil lifts.

source.place: Sentences 4–5: geometric orientation, trace, and the smooth pairing form; rational finite-field realization.

proof.text: At $s$, the fibre functor sends a common-field arrow to the fibre of that same arrow conjugated by the specified sections-scalar comparisons. The naturality theorem for $\iota$ includes compatibility with those sections and Frobenius-pullback comparisons. Therefore, with the endpoints of step 3, $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_N)\iota_N$ is represented by $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,L_1}(\theta_{N,L_1})\iota_{N,L_1}$. The point transport definition makes $\iota$ the exchange-then-transport action; the point normalization identifies the coefficient composite with the canonical constant-unit datum, fixing constant scalars. For the coefficient unit this statement also survives rationalization and common-stage passage by that same normalization. Each chosen vector $\Lambda_s\to N[r]$ is already an arrow from step 1, so these identifications apply to it and to its image under the action.

source.place: Final assertion on Frobenius-equivariant cohomology, with the canonical point transport retained.

proof.text: For each requested equality $w=z$ evaluate both expression trees over $L_1$ as above. Their classes agree in the relevant common-stage Hom group, so its defining equivalence relation gives a finite field $L_{w,z}\supset L_1$ at which the two transported representatives agree. Take $L$ to be the compositum of $L_1$ and these finitely many fields. Functorial scalar extension preserves every equality and all inverse equations from step 2. The scalar-compatible expressions and canonical maps in steps 3–6 identify these transported representatives with the expressions evaluated over $L$. Thus all requested equations hold simultaneously over $L$; no injectivity of any transition on Hom groups has been used.

source.place: Simultaneous descent of finitely many equations implicit in the comparison/cohomology assertions.

proof.text: Conversely, if two finite-stage expressions agree, their morphism classes agree by the defining equivalence relation. Replacing representatives gives eventual equality of each of the finitely many input arrows; move to one common field witnessing them all. The representative formulas of steps 3–6 give identical evaluated expressions there, so their classes are independent of all choices and further extension. Explicitly a degreewise value of a derived pairing $b:A\otimes B\to C$ on vectors $x:\mathbf1\to A[i]$, $y:\mathbf1\to B[j]$ is the composite $\mathbf1\simeq\mathbf1\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{x\otimes y}A[i]\otimes B[j]\simeq(A\otimes B)[i+j]\xrightarrow{b[i+j]}C[i+j]$. All arrows in this finite expression have just been treated. Substituting the action of step 6 proves that any finite-stage identity for these values passes to the common-stage vectors. When $A$ is the compact-support object and $B$ the ordinary object, this formula keeps those two inputs in their original positions and never identifies their functors.

source.place: Final assertion: equations and degreewise pairing values pass to common-stage cohomology.

proof_origin.place: Explicit finite-field assembly of sentences 1–5 and the final cohomology assertion; the common-stage Hom equivalence relation supplies the elementary lifting arguments.
